questions.stem: What are the products of a neutralisation reaction between an acid and a base?
questions.explanation: Neutralisation always produces a salt and water. The general equation is: Acid + Base → Salt + Water. The ionic equation for all acid-alkali neutralisations is H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l).

questions.stem: Neutralisation reactions are best described as:
questions.explanation: Neutralisation reactions are always exothermic, meaning they release heat. The reaction H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O releases approximately 57 kJ per mole of water formed, causing the temperature of the solution to increase.
